region.text: Touraine, created a duchy for Philip the Bold

ledger.note: 1360: the king's son Philip the Bold is created Duke of Touraine: 'He was created Duke of Touraine in 1360' (infobox 'Duke of Touraine 1360–1363'). The state is the apanage, not the royal duchy of 1205, which the crown held ('In 1205, Philip II Augustus of France regained Touraine', Touraine page; reviewer eu-10-f). The kingdom-of-france dossier dates the grant to 1361 (Crown lands page); this page says 1360.

region.text: Touraine, returned to the crown by Philip the Bold

ledger.note: 1363: Philip the Bold gives Touraine back to the crown: 'in 1363, he returned this duchy to the crown' to receive instead the Duchy of Burgundy in apanage (he reigns as Duke of Burgundy from 6 September 1363, infobox).

region.text: Touraine, the duchy of Louis of Orleans

ledger.note: 1386: the king's brother Louis of Orleans becomes Duke of Touraine: 'He was also Duke of Touraine (1386–1392)'. The year is the page's; that the crown gave it to him is my reading, because no page opened says who held Touraine between 1370 (Louis I of Anjou, duke of Touraine in 1370, died 20 September 1384) and 1386.
1392: Louis of Orleans' Touraine title ends ('Duke of Touraine (1386–1392)'); he is Duke of Orleans from 4 June 1392. The page does not say what became of Touraine; the crown is my reading.

region.text: Touraine, the duchy of the Dauphin Charles

ledger.note: 1417: the Dauphin Charles becomes Duke of Touraine and Count of Poitou: infobox 'Duke of Touraine Count of Poitou 1417 – 21 October 1422'. The pages opened do not say who held Touraine between 1392 and 1417.

21 October 1422: Charles succeeds as King Charles VII and the duchy is 'Merged in the crown' (infobox: 'Duke of Touraine Count of Poitou 1417 – 21 October 1422: Vacant Merged in the crown'). The earlier version coded this and the other hand-backs to the crown as renames; the Philip the Bold and Charles VII pages say the duchy returned or merged into the crown, so they are losses and a dissolve. In 1429 he met Joan of Arc at Chinon, in Touraine (Touraine page; she arrived on 23 February 1429, Charles VII page).

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey on the pages opened; the extent is the gazetteer's Touraine (Indre-et-Loire), an approximation of the historical county and duchy.

notes:
Reworked 2026-10-25 after the eu-10-f review (verdict fail). Main correction: the earlier version drew Touraine as a separate state for all of 1205-1491, although the pages put the duchy in the crown's hands for most of those years and the kingdom-of-france dossier draws the same land (about 250 of 286 years overlapped), and coded the hand-backs to the crown as renames. The state is now the apanage only: founded 1360 for Philip the Bold (Philip the Bold page), lost to the crown in 1363; gained 1386 and lost 1392 (Louis of Orleans); gained 1417 and merged into the crown on 21 October 1422 (Charles VII, the dissolve). Between those spans the Cliopatria shapes are verdict wrong with an empty correction (an outline minus itself) and a new keyframe 1392-1416 is empty; the shape 1385 (1385-1421) is empty except where the new keyframes 1386-1391 and 1417-1422 take precedence. The 1205 'found', the Angevin predecessor and the 1491 end of the earlier version are withdrawn: the royal duchy of 1205 stays in kingdom-of-france (decision for the orchestrator: if the 1205 royal duchy is ruled a separate state, kingdom-of-france must drop Touraine and this dossier go back to 1205). The Brétigny sentence (Edward III renounced Normandy, Touraine, Anjou and Maine, Hundred Years' War page) is no longer a war entry: no fighting in Touraine is cited.
Cliopatria's 'County of Touraine' row is not Touraine. Its eight shapes (1206-1304, 1363-1491; 43-47 gazetteer cells) lie on Creuse (24/24 cells) and Haute-Vienne (13/24) with a few Indre, Corrèze and Vienne cells: the County of La Marche and the Limousin, about 150 km from Tours (bbox 0.90-2.60 E, 45.56-46.55 N in shapes.csv). A dossier for the County of La Marche is needed (suggested slug county-of-la-marche, 1206-1491; reuse the Cliopatria 'County of Touraine' polygons as its shapes; the house-of-bourbon dossier already has La Marche events for 1327, 1341 and 1488). The orchestrator decides whether this row becomes that dossier. Without it the La Marche land has no state.
Louis I of Anjou was 'duke of Touraine in 1370' (Louis I of Anjou page; no end, died 20 September 1384): those years are left to house-of-valois-anjou, whose 1370 gain names county-of-touraine as counterpart; since this state does not hold Touraine in 1363-1385 (Philip returned it to the crown in 1363), that counterpart should be kingdom-of-france. kingdom-of-france has a 1361 loss to county-of-touraine (the Philip page says 1360) and no matching return in 1363, 1386/1392 or 1417/1422; its 1250 loss of Touraine to capetian-house-of-anjou is not mirrored here. These are repairs on the France side.
Dates: Touraine confiscated 1204 (Crown lands page, kingdom-of-france) or regained 1205 (Touraine page); apanage to Philip 1361 (kingdom-of-france) or created duke 1360 (Philip the Bold page). Not on the pages: the counts of Touraine before 1205, the apanages of Anjou and Charles of Valois, who held Touraine 1363-1386 other than Louis of Anjou from 1370, 1392-1417 and after 1422 (the review names Archibald Douglas in 1423-24 and Margaret of Scotland's dower; the Charles VII page links a 'John, Duke of Touraine', the Dauphin's brother John, without stating the title), Plessis-lès-Tours. Page budget: 5 pages in the first run, plus Louis I of Anjou in the repair. Gazetteer names needed: none (Touraine and Tours exist).
